sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2012 Nissan GT-R Premium, finished in Deep Blue Pearl with a black interior. The attached Carfax history report lists no mileage discrepancies in this GT-R’s past. It also confirms that this Nissan has been mostly registered in California since new. Factory equipment includes driver-configurable transmission, suspension, and vehicle dynamic control modes, Brembo brake calipers, a body-colored rear spoiler, leather upholstery, heated front seats, a Bose audio system, and cruise control. Modifications reported by the seller are extensive, and the full list is detailed below. Highlights include an AAM Competition valved exhaust system with remote function, AAM Competition 3-inch high flow catted downpipes, AAM Competition upper intercooler pipe kit with twin Tial blow-off valves, an EcuTek ECU tune, Injector Dynamics ID1050X injectors, KW coilovers, 20-inch Vossen Wheels HF-5 wheels, a CarbonTastic steering wheel, and a 14-inch Nifty City head unit with Apple CarPlay capabilities. Called the R35 internally, the GT-R arrived in 2009 as the performance bargain of its decade. It fended off European and American rivals with a hand-built V6 that delivered supercar-like performance, a unique exterior design, an infotainment system developed by the company responsible for the Gran Turismo franchise, and a relatively affordable price tag. Power comes from a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged V6, rated at 530 horsepower and 448 lb-ft of torque in stock form. According to a dyno sheet pictured in the gallery, this GT-R currently produces 634 horsepower and 699 lb-ft of torque at the wheels. Output is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
